stem: Altostrat Media must move large volumes of newly recorded audio and video from legacy on-premises ingestion systems into Cloud Storage every day. Reliability is a top priority, the transfers must not cross the public internet, and the team wants predictable throughput for sustained bulk traffic. Which connectivity design best fits?

choices.text: A Dedicated Interconnect topology with redundant connections in two metropolitan areas, so that ingestion keeps running if one path or one metro is lost
Direct Peering with Google at an edge location, so that the ingestion servers reach the Cloud Storage buckets over private IP addresses
One HA VPN gateway pair over the public internet, with Cloud Router sharing routes, so that encryption is the only protection the traffic needs
A single Dedicated Interconnect connection in one metro with a Classic VPN tunnel as the backup path, so that the redundant path stays cheap to run

stem: A retail group has about forty product teams, each in its own project. A central network team must own subnets, routes and firewall rules, while product teams only deploy workloads into approved subnets. All workloads must talk to each other over internal IP addresses. Which design fits?

choices.text: One VPC network per project joined by Cloud VPN tunnels, with the network team reviewing every team's tunnel settings
A single project for all teams, with Identity and Access Management roles limited to the instances each team creates
Shared VPC with a host project owned by the network team and each product project attached as a service project
VPC Network Peering between every pair of product-team VPC networks, with each team writing its own firewall rules

stem: A software vendor hosts a managed analytics service in its own VPC network on Google Cloud. Hundreds of customers, each with its own VPC network, must consume it privately. Many customer networks use overlapping private ranges, and the vendor does not want customers to reach anything except the service. Which TWO design points fit this requirement? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a VPC Network Peering connection from the vendor network to every customer network
Publish the service behind an internal load balancer through a Private Service Connect service attachment
Merge the vendor and all customer subnets into one Shared VPC network owned by the vendor
Have each customer create a Private Service Connect endpoint with an internal IP address from its own VPC network
Give the service an external IP address and let each customer allowlist the vendor's firewall rules

stem: A manufacturer has four plants, each with its own site network connected to Google Cloud by Cloud Interconnect or HA VPN, and a VPC network holds shared services. The plants also need to exchange data with each other, and the team wants to use the Google network for this instead of buying a separate private WAN. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Cloud NAT gateways in each region so that plants translate their addresses and reach each other through the internet
A full mesh of VPC Network Peering connections between per-plant VPC networks, with each plant's site network behind its own VPC network
Network Connectivity Center as a hub, with each plant's hybrid connection attached as a spoke and site-to-site data transfer enabled
A Private Service Connect endpoint in every plant, so that each site publishes its whole network as a service

stem: Altostrat Media stores a huge, growing archive of audio and video in Cloud Storage. Some episodes become popular years later, so access is unpredictable, and the team does not want to maintain lifecycle rules that guess which objects are cold. Storage cost must fall without lowering availability. Which design fits best?

choices.text: A bucket in the Archive storage class, so that every object gets the lowest storage price regardless of how it is read
A bucket with Autoclass enabled, which moves each object between storage classes automatically according to how it is accessed
A Filestore instance mounted on the editing servers, so that frequently read files stay on high-performance disks
Lifecycle rules that move every object to Coldline after 30 days, so that cost falls on a fixed and predictable schedule

stem: A financial reporting service stores regulatory documents in Cloud Storage. Compliance requires that data stay in two specific European regions, the application must keep working without any path changes if one region fails, and the recovery point objective for new writes should be short and predictable. Which bucket design fits?

choices.text: A dual-region bucket in the two required regions, with turbo replication turned on
A multi-region bucket in the EU location, because it spreads objects across several European regions
A regional bucket in one required region, with a nightly copy job to a regional bucket in the second region
A regional bucket plus Object Versioning, so that earlier versions of objects can be restored after a failure

stem: A growing software-as-a-service team runs its customer data on SQL Server on premises and wants to move to Google Cloud with the lowest administration effort. The application uses T-SQL features and needs a high-availability setup with automatic failover inside one region, but does not need global writes or horizontal scaling beyond a single primary. Which database choice fits?

choices.text: SQL Server on Compute Engine VMs in a managed instance group, so that the team controls the operating system
Bigtable, because it scales writes by adding nodes and removes the need for a relational schema
Spanner, because it replicates across regions and removes the need to think about the database engine
Cloud SQL for SQL Server with a high availability configuration, which fails over to a standby in another zone

stem: A global ticketing platform stores orders in a relational schema and must accept writes from users in North America, Europe and Asia at the same time. Orders need strong consistency and ACID transactions across regions, and the platform must keep serving during a regional outage without manual failover. Which database fits?

choices.text: Spanner in a multi-region configuration, which provides strongly consistent transactions across regions with synchronous replication
Bigtable with multi-cluster replication, which keeps clusters in several regions eventually consistent with one another
Firestore in Datastore mode with one regional location, which scales automatically for key-based reads and writes
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with cross-region read replicas, which serve reads close to users while one primary takes the writes

stem: An automotive supplier collects sensor readings from millions of connected devices, each sending a small record every second. The team needs single-digit-millisecond lookups by device and time range, sustained write rates in the hundreds of thousands per second and no complex joins. Which storage service fits?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, holding all readings in memory with a persistence snapshot
Cloud SQL for MySQL, with one table per device and an index on the timestamp column, on a large primary instance with read replicas
Bigtable, with a row key that starts with the device identifier and ends with a time component
Cloud Storage Standard, with one object per reading and a prefix per device, listed by prefix and time range

stem: A team lifts and shifts a legacy application to Compute Engine. The application expects a shared POSIX file system mounted by several VMs, uses file locking and cannot be changed. The first design stored the files in a Cloud Storage bucket, but the application fails on file semantics. What is the best storage design?

choices.text: A single Persistent Disk attached read-write to every VM in the instance group
Local SSD on each VM, with a scheduled rsync job copying files between the machines
A Cloud Storage bucket mounted through Cloud Storage FUSE, with the application writing files in place
A Filestore instance, exported as an NFS share and mounted by all application VMs

stem: Altostrat Media needs a small piece of code that runs whenever a new video lands in a Cloud Storage bucket. It extracts metadata and writes it to the warehouse, runs for a few seconds per file, and the team wants no servers or clusters to operate and no cost while idle. Which compute choice fits?

choices.text: Compute Engine VMs in a managed instance group that scale on CPU utilization
Cloud Run functions triggered by the bucket event
A Cloud Run job scheduled hourly by Cloud Scheduler, regardless of when files arrive
A GKE Standard cluster with a Deployment that polls the bucket every minute

stem: A platform team runs about thirty microservices on Kubernetes. Several require privileged DaemonSets for a node-level security agent and a specific kernel setting on nodes, and the team already has Kubernetes operations skills. Another team asks which GKE mode fits these workloads. What is the best answer?

choices.text: Cloud Run functions, because each microservice can be wrapped as a function and the nodes disappear
GKE Autopilot, because it is the recommended mode and permits privileged node-level components too
GKE Standard, because it gives control over node configuration and allows the privileged node-level components
Cloud Run, because it runs any container and supports privileged DaemonSets on its own infrastructure

stem: KnightMotives builds a simulation environment to test autonomous-driving software. Thousands of independent simulation runs, each lasting minutes, are queued in batches overnight. A failed run can simply be restarted, and the team wants the lowest compute cost. Which compute choice fits?

choices.text: Sole-tenant nodes reserved for the simulation project, so that other customers never share the hardware
A single very large VM running all simulations in sequence, so that only one machine ever needs patching
Standard on-demand VMs sized for peak load and kept running around the clock, so that no run is ever interrupted
Spot VMs in a managed instance group or a batch service, with jobs written to restart when a VM is preempted

stem: A team moves a legacy application to Compute Engine. The vendor says it needs 8 vCPUs and 40 GB of memory; none of the predefined machine types matches closely, and the memory-heavy sizing would waste money on unused vCPUs. The workload will run for several years at steady load. Which TWO actions reduce cost best? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Select the largest predefined memory-optimized machine type to leave headroom for future growth
Buy resource-based or flexible committed use discounts for the steady, predictable usage
Place the VM in a dual-region location to reduce its hourly price through regional pricing
Run the application only on Spot VMs, since a long-running legacy application restarts cleanly
Create a VM with a custom machine type that has the exact vCPU and memory ratio the vendor needs

stem: EHR Healthcare must ingest claims and clinical updates from new provider partners. Volumes spike unpredictably, events arrive continuously, records must be cleaned and enriched within seconds, and the results land in BigQuery for analytics. The team wants no clusters to size. Which processing design fits?

choices.text: Pub/Sub to receive events, a streaming Dataflow pipeline to transform them, and BigQuery as the destination
Compute Engine VMs running a self-written consumer, with a fixed number of instances behind a load balancer
A Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster that is created manually each morning and sized for the expected peak
A nightly batch export of all partner files to Cloud Storage, followed by a scheduled BigQuery load job

stem: Cymbal Retail wants shoppers to find products by typing natural-language questions on its website and app, with results ranked using the catalog and shopper behavior. The team prefers a managed service tuned to retail over building its own search stack. Which product choice fits?

choices.text: AI Commerce Search in Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience, the managed retail search service
Memorystore for Redis holding a copy of the catalog, queried with exact-match key lookups
Cloud Storage with a static index file for every product category, which the browser downloads and filters locally
BigQuery with a LIKE query over product titles, exposed through a custom web service

stem: A bank wants to extract fields from thousands of scanned loan applications with fixed layouts (names, addresses, amounts) into structured records, with confidence scores so that low-confidence documents can be routed to a human reviewer in the bank's own workflow. Which AI product choice fits best?

choices.text: Cloud Translation, because it can read text in scanned images and return it in a chosen language
Document AI, with a processor for the document type and a review queue fed by low confidence scores
Training a custom image classification model on Compute Engine GPUs to label the scans by document type
Prompting a general chat model by hand for every scanned page, and copying answers into a spreadsheet

stem: A research lab wants to pretrain a large custom model on its own data, with a distributed job running across hundreds of accelerators for weeks and needing high-bandwidth, low-latency networking and fast storage. Which infrastructure choice fits?

choices.text: A fleet of general-purpose E2 VMs in a managed instance group, trained with the CPU only
Calling a hosted Gemini model through the Gemini API with a long prompt that includes the training data
AI Hypercomputer, using GPU or TPU clusters with high-performance networking and parallel storage
Cloud Run services with GPUs attached, scaled out as one instance per accelerator

stem: Altostrat Media wants a 24/7 support chat assistant that answers viewer questions using only the company's own program guides and policies, cites the source of each answer, and does not invent shows that do not exist. Which TWO design choices fit this goal? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Train a new foundation model from scratch on the guides using AI Hypercomputer GPU clusters
Turn off all grounding and rely on a higher sampling temperature to make answers more varied and engaging
Fine-tune a model once on a snapshot of the guides and expect it to know every later schedule change
Ground the model's answers in the company's documents using a managed retrieval-augmented generation setup, such as Agent Search over the guides
Build the assistant with Conversational Agents or an agent on the Agent Platform, using a foundation model such as Gemini

stem: EHR Healthcare runs containerized applications on several Kubernetes clusters in Google Cloud and on premises, managed by different teams with different configurations. Past outages came from misconfiguration. The company wants consistent policy, configuration and visibility across all clusters. Which design fits?

choices.text: Replace Kubernetes with Compute Engine VMs and manage them with startup scripts that each team edits locally
Register the clusters in a fleet with GKE Enterprise, and apply shared configuration and policy through fleet features
Move all workloads into one very large cluster in a single region, so that there is only one configuration to maintain
Keep each cluster independent and document the standard settings in a shared wiki page for the teams to follow

stem: A company runs batch analytics on private Compute Engine VMs and on-premises servers. Security rules say none of these machines may have external IP addresses, yet all of them must call Google APIs such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery without traffic crossing the public internet. The on-premises servers connect to the VPC network through Cloud Interconnect. Which design fits?

choices.text: Enable Private Google Access on the VM subnets, and point on-premises hosts at the Private Google Access virtual IPs over the Interconnect
Assign external IP addresses to all VMs and restrict egress with firewall rules, because Google APIs need a public address
Create a Classic VPN tunnel from every on-premises server straight to the Cloud Storage service endpoint
Create a separate VPC Network Peering connection between the on-premises network and Google's API network

stem: An architect is turning a retailer's workshop notes into a requirements document. Which TWO of the following statements are non-functional requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Customers must be able to save several delivery addresses in their account profile
The warehouse team must be able to export the daily picking list as a spreadsheet file
Support agents must be able to refund a single line item from an order that they are viewing on screen
The order service must keep accepting orders when one zone of its region is unavailable
Checkout pages must respond within a set time at the 95th percentile during promotions

stem: A parcel-tracking company runs a customer portal, a driver dispatch system and an internal HR portal. The board asks for a business continuity plan that is affordable. A workshop shows that a dispatch outage stops revenue within minutes, the customer portal can tolerate a few hours of downtime, and the HR portal can be unavailable for days. What should the architect do first when shaping the continuity design?

choices.text: Defer all continuity design until after migration, then apply the cheapest backup schedule to every workload to keep the budget simple
Ask each application team to choose its own continuity design independently, then merge the results without comparing them to business impact
Run a business impact analysis, then give each system its own recovery time and recovery point targets
Deploy every system with the strongest multi-region active-active design, so the same continuity target applies to all workloads without exception

stem: EHR Healthcare promised hospitals at least 99.9% availability. In the draft design, a customer-facing request passes in series through the web tier, an API tier and a database, and each of the three has its own availability objective of 99.9%. What should the architect tell management about the promise?

choices.text: The combined availability of the chain is lower than 99.9%, so tighten the dependency targets or add redundancy
The promise is met, because each component individually reaches the 99.9% target that was stated
The promise is irrelevant, because availability objectives apply only to the database and not to the whole request path
The promise is met, because adding more serial components makes the chain more reliable than any single one

stem: A SaaS company will run about the same number of vCPUs and amount of memory in one region on Compute Engine for the next three years. Another team's workloads, on a different machine series and in other regions, change every few months. The finance lead wants the biggest discount that does not risk paying for unused commitments. Which plan fits?

choices.text: Buy no commitments and rely on on-demand rates for both teams, since commitments cannot be matched to a changing set of workloads
Buy three-year resource commitments for the variable team's current machine series in each region it uses
Buy resource-based commitments for the steady footprint and a modest flexible commitment for the variable part
Buy one large spend-based commitment sized to the peak of both teams, because a spend commitment is always cheaper than a resource commitment

stem: A company moving to Google Cloud has three product teams that share one billing account. Executives want each team to see its own spend, receive warnings before a monthly limit is exceeded, and be able to trigger automated responses to a runaway cost. Which TWO actions support this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Move every team into one project so that only a single budget needs to be maintained
Disable billing on the shared account whenever any team approaches its target, so that all spending stops at once
Ask each team to read the monthly invoice and report increases manually, which avoids any tooling
Apply consistent labels or separate projects per team so billing data can be broken down by team and exported for analysis
Create per-team Cloud Billing budgets with alert thresholds and use the notifications to trigger automated responses

stem: Cymbal Retail exchanges orders with suppliers through nightly SFTP file drops and batch ETL, and a failure in one step silently delays everything after it. The business wants new gen AI catalog enrichment and order tracking to react as events happen, and wants to add consumers later without changing producers. Which integration pattern best meets this?

choices.text: Load all data into one shared relational database and let each application read the tables it needs at any time
Publish business events to Pub/Sub topics and let each consumer subscribe independently
Have each producing application call every consuming application's API synchronously and wait for each reply
Keep the nightly files but have every consumer poll the SFTP server each minute to cut the delay between the steps

stem: A logistics firm runs an on-premises PostgreSQL database for shipment tracking. Analysts need the data in BigQuery within seconds of each change, the source must keep serving the live application, and the team wants no servers of its own to run for the replication. Which approach should the architect choose?

choices.text: Run a self-managed replication tool on Compute Engine virtual machines that the team itself patches, monitors and scales
Rewrite the application so that it writes every record to BigQuery and the database at the same time
Schedule a nightly full export of every table to files and load them to BigQuery with a batch job
Use Datastream change data capture into BigQuery over private VPN or Interconnect connectivity

stem: A broadcaster must copy hundreds of terabytes of archived video from its on-premises NAS to Cloud Storage over an existing 1 Gbps link that also carries daily business traffic. Past ad hoc copies using scripts stalled and were restarted by hand. Leadership wants a reliable, scheduled, verifiable transfer that can be throttled during working hours. Which solution fits?

choices.text: Storage Transfer Service with on-premises agents, scheduling, retries and bandwidth limits
A single long-running copy script on one workstation that is restarted by an operator after every interruption
Streaming each file through Pub/Sub messages so the broker handles retry and bandwidth sharing for the copy
Mounting the Cloud Storage bucket on each employee's laptop so that editors can drag and drop the video files straight into it

stem: KnightMotives wants a CRM and dealer toolset covering sales, service and inventory. The company's in-house teams are stretched by fragmented legacy code and technical debt, dealers have no budget for new equipment, and the business wants value within months. Which disposition best balances time to value and risk?

choices.text: Modify the legacy dealer application in place by adding new modules to its existing code base and servers
Deprecate the dealer tooling without replacement, because dealers can use spreadsheets until the new data platform is complete
Buy a browser-based dealer-management and CRM product and integrate it through APIs
Build a custom CRM from scratch with the in-house teams so that every feature matches current internal processes exactly

stem: EHR Healthcare is moving customer-facing systems to Google Cloud and promised hospitals at least 99.9% availability. Management also wants proof that the move is paying off after one year. Which set of key performance indicators best fits these goals?

choices.text: Count of alert emails sent per month and the number of dashboards created in the monitoring tool
Monthly availability of customer-facing services against the 99.9% target, plus unit cost per practice versus the colocation baseline
Total number of virtual machines created, number of projects in the organization and number of engineers who completed training courses each quarter
Total count of services migrated, regardless of their availability, cost or the number of incidents after migration

stem: In a requirements workshop, a media start-up's product owner asks for "the lowest possible latency worldwide, the highest availability, and the lowest possible cost". The architect knows these goals pull against each other. What is the best next step?

choices.text: Choose the highest availability design with global multi-region replication, since cost can be reduced later without redesigning it
Quantify each goal with the business as a latency percentile, an availability target and a cost ceiling, then rank them
Record all three goals as written and let the engineering team decide the trade-offs during implementation without further review
Choose the lowest cost design, because availability and latency can be improved after launch simply by adding more servers to it

stem: A manufacturer compares keeping its data center against moving a steady ERP-reporting workload to Google Cloud. The CFO asks for a fair business case. Which analysis is most defensible?

choices.text: Compare only the list price of equivalent virtual machines to the purchase price of servers, and ignore all other items
Treat the on-premises hardware as free since it is already purchased, and compare only the cloud bill with zero
Compare the monthly cloud bill to server depreciation alone, ignoring facilities, staffing and migration effort
Compare the full multi-year cost of both options, including refresh, facility, staff, cloud run costs and migration effort

stem: KnightMotives plans to replace its mainframe supply-chain and ERP system gradually, because a big-bang cutover could halt plants and dealers. Which approach to the future improvement of this system reduces risk the most?

choices.text: Copy the mainframe to virtual machines unchanged and declare the modernization finished, since the hardware is then gone
Let each plant choose and build its own replacement on its own timeline, so no central design is needed
Put an API layer in front of the legacy system, move one capability at a time behind it and retire legacy parts as traffic moves
Freeze legacy changes for years while a full replacement is built, then switch all plants over in one weekend

stem: Cymbal Retail's pilot for gen AI product descriptions produced good drafts, and the merchandising lead wants to extend it to the whole catalog next month. Wrong descriptions would reach customers directly, and compliance reviewers have not seen the process. What should the architect recommend for the next phase?

choices.text: Expand in stages with human review before catalog updates, measuring accuracy and rejection rates at each step
Stop the program until models never produce an error, since any human review proves that the approach is unsuitable
Publish every generated description for the entire catalog automatically and fix errors when customers complain
Replace the pilot with a hand-written description process for every product, to avoid any new risk from automation

stem: An architect reviews a platform that has run on Google Cloud for two years. The team wants a standing way to find savings in idle and oversized resources and to feed them into the improvement backlog. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Wait for a cost spike on the invoice, then ask engineers to guess which resources are the cause
Ignore recommendations and rely on a yearly purchase of a larger commitment to lower the unit price of everything
Review Active Assist recommendations regularly, weigh saving against risk and schedule accepted changes in the backlog
Apply every recommendation automatically on the day it appears, in all environments, with no owner review or testing first

stem: A platform team learns that the Container Registry service it uses for build images has been shut down and that Cloud Deployment Manager has reached end of support. The roadmap has no time for platform work. What does this show about planning future improvements, and what is the best response?

choices.text: Treat each retirement as an emergency, pause all feature work and migrate everything at once in a single release
Track deprecation notices and migrate to the supported replacement, such as Artifact Registry, on a schedule
Pin all pipelines to the retired tool and write private scripts to emulate it, so that nothing needs to change
Retirements can be ignored because running workloads continue indefinitely without any change to them at all

stem: An architect is asked to propose a new analytics capability for next year's roadmap. A promising Google Cloud feature is labelled Preview in the documentation. The capability would support a regulated production workload with contractual availability targets. What is the best way to treat the feature in the roadmap?

choices.text: Exclude every Preview feature from all future planning, including proofs of concept and vendor conversations
Build the production design around it and plan to replace it quickly if it is retired, so no testing is required
Adopt it for production immediately, because every Google Cloud feature has the same support commitments as a generally available one
Evaluate it in a non-production proof of concept and commit production use only after general availability

stem: A company has a list of eight improvement ideas for its Google Cloud platform: reduce toil in deployments, pay down database schema debt, add a new language to the mobile app, refactor a rarely used admin tool, and so on. The platform team can deliver only three this quarter. Which TWO practices produce the best prioritisation? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Weigh dependencies, so that enabling work that unblocks several other improvements is sequenced early
Postpone all technical debt until a calm period, since debt does not accumulate interest like financial debt
Always start with the cheapest items, regardless of what they achieve, to show progress in the number of tickets closed
Fund the items whose owners argue most loudly, since seniority indicates the importance of each item
Score items on business value, risk reduced and effort, favouring those that address measured incidents and delays

stem: After launching a new subscription service, a team's backlog fills with reliability work and new features, and nobody agrees which to do. The service has an availability objective, and the monthly data show that the service has consumed most of its error budget by mid-month. How should the architect use this data to plan improvements?

choices.text: Shift the next iteration toward reliability work until the error budget is no longer being consumed too fast
Continue shipping features at full pace, since the error budget is only a reporting number that has no bearing on planning
Remove the objective entirely, because it creates conflict between feature work and reliability work
Raise the availability objective to a stricter value so that the remaining budget looks larger

stem: EHR Healthcare wants insights and predictions from provider data, and many new providers will send data in different formats over the next two years. The architects are proposing a roadmap. Which sequence is the most sensible?

choices.text: Keep each provider's data in its own separate database indefinitely and run reports by hand on request
Postpone all analytics until every provider has migrated to one common data format, and offer no insights before then
Train predictive models on whatever each provider sends, then design ingestion and quality processes afterwards
Centralise ingestion and governed storage with quality checks, then build analytics, then add predictive models

stem: A company's roadmap for the next three years lists features that must be portable between cloud providers if its strategy changes. A team suggests building the order database on a proprietary managed service because its performance is the best. How should the architect treat portability in this decision?

choices.text: Require identical architectures to run unchanged on two providers at all times, so that any workload can move at any time
Ignore portability completely, because switching providers is never a realistic possibility for any company
Weigh lock-in cost against benefit, using portable interfaces only where exit risk is material and managed services elsewhere
Avoid every managed service and run self-managed open source software everywhere to eliminate any dependency

stem: A news site's traffic is highly spiky: a few viral stories cause bursts that last minutes, and most of the day it runs at a fraction of its peak. It runs on a fixed fleet of virtual machines sized for the peak, and the CFO asks the architect for the next-year improvement with the greatest cost effect and the least operational work. Which proposal is best?

choices.text: Keep the fleet unchanged and add a second identical fleet in another region so that every peak is shared between the two
Move the stateless front end to a serverless or autoscaled platform and keep a small latency-critical baseline
Reduce the fleet to the average load size permanently and accept slow pages during viral peaks
Buy a three-year commitment on the entire fixed fleet at peak size, to get the discount on all of the capacity

stem: Twelve months after a platform migration, leadership asks how to decide what to improve next. Which TWO sources give the architect the most reliable evidence for the next roadmap? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The number of new Google Cloud products announced in the last year, since adopting more of them shows platform maturity
The original project plan, since it already defined all improvements that will ever be required
The preferences of the most senior stakeholder, as expressed in the next steering meeting
A post-implementation review that compares the KPIs set before the project with the values measured now
Operational telemetry such as incidents, latency, error rates and cost reports from the running platform, trended over time

stem: A company adopts a cloud-first policy. A year later, a regional hospital group's imaging system, which depends on a certified on-premises device and a 10 ms link to the scanners, is proposed for migration. How should the architect apply the policy?

choices.text: Move it immediately, because any exception to a cloud-first policy weakens it and creates precedent for others
Exempt every workload that has ever had a special requirement, so that most of the estate stays on-premises
Treat cloud-first as a default: keep this workload on-premises with hybrid connectivity and revisit later
Rewrite the policy so no workload may remain on-premises and press the vendor to certify the device in the cloud
